title: The window
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Tuesday. The owner lets him do the window. He arranges twelve empty frames in it, nothing inside any of them. She looks at it a long time and leaves it that way for a year.

panels.composition: The frame shop's window from inside. WOOD arranging frames on the display shelf: twelve, all sizes, all empty.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a young man arranging a dozen empty picture frames of different sizes in a shop's front window display

panels.composition: From the sidewalk on 101: the window. Twelve empty frames, and through each one, a piece of the shop, the owner, the mat cutter, the road reflected. The town, framed, in pieces.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, a frame shop's front window seen from the sidewalk with twelve empty frames arranged so each one frames a different piece of the shop interior and the reflected road, no words
image.notes: Each empty frame frames something. The strip's first composition about composition.

panels.composition: The OWNER outside on the sidewalk, arms folded, looking at it. A long time.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, an older woman standing on a sidewalk with her arms folded looking at a shop window, no words

panels.composition: Inside. The owner coming back in. Wood waiting.

balloons.text: Leave it. People will bring their own.

image.prompt: brush-pen black-and-white, xerox grain, an older woman coming back into a frame shop and speaking to a young man who was waiting for a verdict

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Twelve empty frames. 'People will bring their own.' It stays a year.
